name: known per-example losses and all reductions
input: one positive and one negative prediction
test:
import math
import torch
y = torch.tensor([1, 0])
p = torch.tensor([0.9, 0.2], dtype=torch.float64)
expected = p.new_tensor([-0.25 * 0.1**2 * math.log(0.9), -0.75 * 0.2**2 * math.log(0.8)])
for reduction in ('none', 'sum', 'mean'):
    actual = binary_focal_loss(y, p, reduction=reduction)
    want = expected if reduction == 'none' else getattr(expected, reduction)()
    assert isinstance(actual, torch.Tensor) and actual.shape == want.shape
    assert actual.dtype == p.dtype and actual.device == p.device
    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, want, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-15)

name: alpha gamma and label-dependent weights across a matrix
input: non-default hyperparameters; easy and hard examples; reductions over every axis
test:
import math
import torch
y = torch.tensor([[1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 0]])
p = torch.tensor([[.95, .15, .05], [.85, .55, .45]], dtype=torch.float64)
before = (y.clone(), p.clone())
for alpha, gamma in ((.25, 2.), (.6, 1.5), (.03, .5), (.9, 4.)):
    values = []
    for label, prob in zip(y.flatten().tolist(), p.flatten().tolist()):
        pt, weight = (prob, alpha) if label else (1-prob, 1-alpha)
        values.append(-weight * (1-pt)**gamma * math.log(pt))
    expected = p.new_tensor(values).reshape_as(p)
    for reduction in ('none', 'sum', 'mean'):
        actual = binary_focal_loss(y, p, alpha, gamma, reduction)
        want = expected if reduction == 'none' else getattr(expected, reduction)()
        assert actual.shape == want.shape and actual.dtype == p.dtype
        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, want, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-15)
assert torch.equal(y, before[0]) and torch.equal(p, before[1])

name: singleton dimensions label dtypes and floating dtype preservation
input: rank-three singleton inputs and bool/int/float labels in float32 and float64
test:
import math
import torch
for dtype in (torch.float32, torch.float64):
    for label_dtype in (torch.bool, torch.long, torch.float32):
        p = torch.tensor([[[.25]]], dtype=dtype, requires_grad=True)
        for label in (0, 1):
            y = torch.full((1, 1, 1), label, dtype=label_dtype)
            pt, weight = (.25, .37) if label else (.75, .63)
            expected = p.new_tensor(-weight * (1-pt)**1.5 * math.log(pt))
            for reduction in ('none', 'sum', 'mean'):
                loss = binary_focal_loss(y, p, .37, 1.5, reduction)
                assert isinstance(loss, torch.Tensor) and loss.dtype == dtype and loss.device == p.device
                assert loss.shape == (p.shape if reduction == 'none' else torch.Size([]))
                torch.testing.assert_close(loss.reshape(()), expected)

name: analytic probability gradients and upstream weights for every reduction
input: both labels; non-default hyperparameters; input preservation after backward
test:
import torch
y = torch.tensor([[1, 0], [0, 1]])
base = torch.tensor([[.2, .3], [.8, .65]], dtype=torch.float64)
alpha, gamma = .37, 1.5
for reduction in ('none', 'sum', 'mean'):
    p = base.clone().requires_grad_()
    before = (p.detach().clone(), y.clone())
    loss = binary_focal_loss(y, p, alpha, gamma, reduction)
    assert loss.requires_grad and loss.dtype == p.dtype
    with torch.no_grad():
        pos = alpha * (gamma*(1-p)**(gamma-1)*p.log() - (1-p)**gamma/p)
        neg = (1-alpha) * (-gamma*p**(gamma-1)*torch.log1p(-p) + p**gamma/(1-p))
        expected = torch.where(y == 1, pos, neg)
    if reduction == 'none':
        upstream = p.new_tensor([[1., -2.], [.5, 3.]])
        got, = torch.autograd.grad(loss, p, upstream)
        expected = expected * upstream
    else:
        got, = torch.autograd.grad(loss, p)
        if reduction == 'mean': expected = expected / p.numel()
    torch.testing.assert_close(got, expected, rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-12)
    assert torch.equal(p.detach(), before[0]) and torch.equal(y, before[1])

name: gradcheck on noncontiguous probabilities
input: double precision numerical differentiation with fractional gamma
test:
import torch
p = torch.tensor([[.2, .4], [.7, .6], [.3, .8]], dtype=torch.float64).T.requires_grad_()
y = torch.tensor([[1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 0]]).T
assert not p.is_contiguous() and not y.is_contiguous()
for reduction in ('none', 'sum', 'mean'):
    fn = lambda value: binary_focal_loss(y, value, .6, 1.5, reduction)
    assert torch.autograd.gradcheck(fn, (p,), eps=1e-6, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)

name: near-boundary probabilities remain finite without clipping
input: hard examples near zero and one; float32 and float64 losses and gradients
test:
import math
import torch
for dtype, small in ((torch.float32, 1e-6), (torch.float64, 1e-12)):
    p = torch.tensor([small, 1-small, small, 1-small], dtype=dtype, requires_grad=True)
    y = torch.tensor([1, 0, 0, 1])
    expected = []
    for label, value in zip(y.tolist(), p.detach().tolist()):
        if label:
            expected.append(-.3 * (1-value)**1.5 * math.log(value))
        else:
            expected.append(-.7 * value**1.5 * math.log1p(-value))
    loss = binary_focal_loss(y, p, .3, 1.5, 'none')
    assert torch.isfinite(loss).all()
    torch.testing.assert_close(loss, p.new_tensor(expected), rtol=2e-5, atol=0.)
    grad, = torch.autograd.grad(loss.sum(), p)
    assert torch.isfinite(grad).all() and torch.all(grad != 0)
# A clipping epsilon would change this hard-example loss and its gradient.
p = torch.tensor([1e-200], dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
loss = binary_focal_loss(torch.tensor([1]), p)
torch.testing.assert_close(loss, p.new_tensor(-.25*math.log(1e-200)), rtol=1e-12, atol=0.)
grad, = torch.autograd.grad(loss, p)
torch.testing.assert_close(grad, p.new_tensor([-.25/1e-200]), rtol=1e-12, atol=0.)

name: device preservation on CPU and available accelerators
input: float32 loss and probability gradient remain on the input device
test:
import math
import torch
devices = ['cpu']
if torch.cuda.is_available(): devices.append('cuda')
if torch.backends.mps.is_available(): devices.append('mps')
for device in devices:
    p = torch.tensor([.25, .75], dtype=torch.float32, device=device, requires_grad=True)
    y = torch.tensor([1, 0], device=device)
    loss = binary_focal_loss(y, p, .3, 1.5, 'none')
    assert loss.device == p.device and loss.dtype == p.dtype and loss.shape == p.shape
    expected = p.new_tensor([-.3*.75**1.5*math.log(.25), -.7*.75**1.5*math.log(.25)])
    torch.testing.assert_close(loss, expected)
    grad, = torch.autograd.grad(loss.sum(), p)
    assert grad.device == p.device and torch.isfinite(grad).all()
